[USER] User is looking for affordable snack options to bring to work instead of buying a muffin every morning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested affordable snack options include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Fresh Fruits: Apples, bananas, oranges, or seasonal fruits, costing around $5 for a bag lasting a week.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Nuts and Seeds: Almonds, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, or sunflower seeds, costing around $5-$10 for a bag lasting a few weeks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Energy Balls: Made with rolled oats, peanut butter, and honey, easy to prepare and store for up to a week.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Granola: Costs around $3-$5 for a bag lasting a few weeks; store-brand options or homemade recommended.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Dried Fruits and Veggies: Dried apricots, cranberries, carrots, and sweet potato chips costing around $2-$5.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Oatmeal: Costs around $2-$5 for a bag; can be packed with nuts, seeds, or dried fruits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Hard-Boiled Eggs: Boil a dozen eggs on the weekend for a quick protein-rich snack.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Canned Goods: Canned tuna, beans, or chicken costing around $1-$2 per can.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Homemade Trail Mix: Mix nuts, seeds, and dried fruits; can add chocolate chips.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Yogurt: Individual cups costing around $1-$2; store-brand options or bulk buying recommended.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tips to save more include buying in bulk, using coupons, packing snacks in reusable containers, and meal prepping on weekends.
